reviews.text:
I was able to see the head veterinarian.

It was a Sunday, so I was relieved that there were no other hospitals open. It was also very helpful that they don't require appointments, so I could just wait my turn and be seen.

The treatment costs aren't cheap, are they? It's a veterinary hospital after all... it's over 10,000 yen...
If I had one request, it would be to limit the number of people. The waiting room is small, and if two or three family members come, there's no place to sit, so they have to stand. I'd like to request that only one accompanying person be allowed.

As other reviews have mentioned, it seems they are not skilled in eye treatment.

My elderly dog's eye was swollen, and I took him to this clinic, but the vet himself admitted it wasn't his specialty. He said he would consult with a vet he knew who was skilled in eye treatment, but that vet was busy that day and couldn't see us. So, he prescribed four different eye drops and instructed me to administer them every five minutes.

Four different drops, especially for an elderly dog. There was even a steroid eye drop, and when I asked if it was okay, he just told me to follow the instructions.

The swelling didn't subside, and I went back for a second visit three days later.

It seemed he had consulted with his vet friend, but was told to handle it myself. When I complained about the four different eye drops, he retorted, half-angrily, that it wasn't his specialty.

Ultimately, my dog ​​went blind within about a week.

Perhaps it was inevitable that he would go blind, but
I still regret that there might have been a better treatment option. I wonder if the outcome would have been different if I had gone to a different hospital.

In any case, I cannot forgive the doctor who proceeded with uncertain treatment despite knowing that he was not proficient in that area.
I've been helped many times by their accurate diagnoses.

Thank you so much for your continued support.

The doctor is very kind and thorough, and is very careful about how they speak to you.

The assistants are also very kind, making this a very pleasant animal hospital to visit. I've been going there for 5 years, and the doctor has changed about 3 times, so I hope they can find a permanent replacement.

I am truly grateful for the care I received from the staff at this hospital and pet hotel. The doctors and staff are always kind and gentle with animals, and while I have many dogs and cats, I have used this facility many times since my first two hamsters were babies, whenever something happened. Dr. Horiguchi carefully monitored my pets, even though there was little he could do for treatment. He patiently answered all my questions, and they were able to survive severe pneumonia and hang on for three months, even though they eventually developed tumors and passed away. Both pets passed away peacefully at two years and two years and eight months old, without suffering much, and with smiles on their faces. It's all thanks to you all, even though it's a little late, but thank you so much! The hotel staff also always upload videos, and when I pick them up and see how they look when they come home, I can always rest assured that they were well cared for. Thank you! If I ever have the chance to adopt a pet, I would definitely use this facility.

I'm glad I was able to have them treated here!

I used to go to a different hospital in the same group, but after moving, I started having my pet treated by Dr. Horiguchi here.

Recently, my elderly dog ​​passed away from aspiration pneumonia, and I was so grateful for the support Dr. Horiguchi and his staff provided to both my dog ​​and me.

I believe that being able to let my dog ​​pass away peacefully at home, surrounded by my family, and having fewer regrets now, is all thanks to Dr. Horiguchi and his staff.

Thank you so much.

This hospital group has its own insurance, which makes medical expenses more affordable.

I know that veterinary hospitals are expensive, and some people don't like the idea of ​​tests being performed, but
I trust Dr. Horiguchi more than any other doctor I've seen.

I've seen pets die at hospitals that look nice on the outside but don't perform proper tests, so I was very grateful that they could perform tests immediately here.

Please take care of yourselves and keep up the good work.

Thank you so much for everything.

They are very kind and helpful.

Both the doctor and staff seem to love animals, and their interactions with them make it clear that they do. In fact, my Shiba Inu was very calm during the examination.

Their examinations, diagnoses, and treatments are always accurate, and I trust them completely. I've also had other doctors see my pet, and they've all been very pleasant and helpful.

I hope to continue using their services in the future.

I went there because Sumire had been taking care of them.

My rescue cat was about 3 months old, and had been unwell, so we had been delaying her vaccinations.

They gave me an irrelevant diagnosis, took X-rays and ultrasounds without my consent, and charged me a huge amount. They even threatened to hospitalize my extremely weak cat and perform a CT scan under general anesthesia. They even attached tubes to my hand…
The blood test results showed a decrease in white blood cells.

When I consulted a different hospital, they immediately identified the suspicious condition and asked why they hadn't noticed the low white blood cell count…
The tests revealed feline parvovirus.

She passed away that morning.

I'm glad we didn't hospitalize her.

I will never go there again.

This is just one example, so please refer to other reviews before making your decision.
The summary and background are described above.

Summary
In my opinion, if your cat is diagnosed with a serious illness at this hospital in the future, I recommend seeking a second opinion at a larger hospital.
Don't be complacent just because it's nearby.
It might be okay to use it for vaccinations and preventative care.

Below are the reasons and background for giving it one star.

My cat wasn't feeling well, so I took her to this hospital, and it was quickly determined that she had a life-threatening illness.
After continuing treatment for a certain period, her condition only worsened, so I sought a second opinion at another hospital.

At the other hospital:
- A misdiagnosis was discovered.
- The doctor strongly stated that the medication dosage was the minimum amount.

Comparing the explanation of the cause and treatment methods, I felt it was extremely sloppy.

Because:
The other hospital performed blood tests and ultrasound examinations, just like this hospital, and based on the results, the root cause was identified.
This root cause went into more detail than the explanation given at this hospital.

Furthermore, they mentioned the unlikely possibility that multiple internal organs might be the cause, and prescribed medication that considered all possible causes.

However, the medication prescribed at this hospital was for organs that did not correspond to any of the possible causes.

Therefore, treatment was delayed, and the day after being examined at another hospital, I was given medication typically prescribed for terminal illnesses.

I suspect that this hospital explained a "vague cause" to the patient and, when choosing a treatment, could only administer the minimum necessary medication.

Considering that it was "early detection," I highly doubt that this hospital considered "complete cure and remission" from the beginning.

To be honest, I think they are "quack doctors."

I also considered this hospital, but the reviews there mentioned not only poor treatment methods but also bad attitudes from the reception staff, suggesting that the entire organization might be corrupt.

I found another hospital by researching the diagnosis explained at this hospital and finding hospitals with a history of multiple treatments through blogs.

Every pet owner wants to provide the best possible support as this is the last act of filial piety they can show their partner.

Please consider this once again.
Thank you for your continued support. The teachers are also kind.
Thank you for listening to me so attentively. I would like to continue receiving your care in the future.
I'm taking my hamster to this vet. They were able to find things that other vets couldn't figure out, and they explained the symptoms very carefully.

I've been a patient at Sumire Animal Hospital for many years. While the previous head veterinarian has changed, the current veterinarian has continued to provide excellent and caring care, offering thorough examinations from various perspectives when necessary, which gave me peace of mind. They carefully explained treatment methods and medications, and patiently answered any questions I had. In particular, when my pet's appetite decreased, they considered multiple options, which was incredibly helpful. Thank you very much.

My pet underwent surgery in the past, but was able to live a long life, so I'm very grateful for the outcome.

The staff seemed well-balanced and many were very kind.

I've also used their pet grooming service, and they were very convenient, sometimes arranging for a consultation after grooming depending on the time. They were attentive and noticed changes in my pet's skin during grooming, showing great care.

I haven't been there for a while, but I hope to have my pet examined there again if the opportunity arises.

I hope this place continues to be a great animal hospital for many years to come.

The director has changed, but about four years ago, the director was Dr. Seiji Koge (currently working at Osaka Animal Medical Center).

I went to the clinic for a while to care for three rescued kittens who were dying from cat flu, and my older Pomeranian, who was stressed out by the kittens and had bloody stools. However, both were misdiagnosed, and I ended up wasting about 200,000 yen in medical fees.

I'll explain the details below.

******************

I rescued three kittens who were dying and had siblings lying on the side of the road. Their eyes had been severely damaged by the cat flu, and one of them had a painful, bulging eye.

I was searching online for a hospital within commuting distance that had some expertise in ophthalmology, and I found Dr. Seiji Koge, then the director of Fukushima Chuo, in his profile, which listed ophthalmology as his specialty. I went to see him, and despite repeated visits, my kittens' eyes didn't improve at all.

So I searched online for a veterinary hospital with an ophthalmology department, and after seeing an ophthalmologist, his bulging eye finally returned to its normal position.

By the way, when I showed the eye ointment prescribed by Dr. Hige to the doctor, he told me to stop using it immediately because it would make the condition worse. So, going to Fukushima Chuo only made the condition worse, not better.

Also, after rescuing the kitten, our 8-year-old Pomeranian started having bloody urine and stools, probably due to stress, so I took him to Dr. Hige for an examination while the kitten was in for an appointment.

During that examination, an "enlarged prostate" and "kidney stones" were diagnosed, and the treatment was as follows:

● Enlarged prostate: Neutering was recommended
● Stones: Supplements were prescribed

However, when I took him back for a follow-up examination after giving him the supplements, I was told that the number of stones had increased.

Despite this, the same supplements were prescribed, which left me feeling suspicious.

I also had a blood test done at Fukushima Chuo to evaluate my prostate for enlargement, as I was planning to have it removed. However, the blood test also showed a problem, so I was prescribed a different supplement. I was concerned about just being prescribed supplements, so I had another test at another hospital.

To my surprise, the results showed that there were absolutely no kidney stones.

At Fukushima Chuo, they even said that the number of kidney stones had increased, but when I went to another hospital a few days later, there were zero.

I asked the doctor
"At the previous hospital (Fukushima Chuo), both tests found stones, and the second test even said that the number of stones had increased. Are you sure there aren't any?"

To which the doctor replied
"I did a thorough test with that in mind, but they couldn't find any."

As for the enlarged prostate, since he's 8 years old and quite old, it may have grown a little, but it's not enlarged, and there's no problem with leaving it as it is.

A month later, I went back to the same hospital for another kidney stone test, and again the result was zero, so no treatment or castration surgery was necessary.

By the way, the hospital I went to later had newer testing equipment and was able to show me the results clearly on a larger computer screen, so it seemed unlikely that they had missed anything.

At Fukushima Chuo, the ultrasound image was a small, poor quality printout, so it was very difficult to see.

I was annoyed at how careless the doctor was, but at the same time, it made me realize once again how important a second opinion is.

Thank you for your continued support.

I always appreciate your kind and thorough service; it puts me at ease.
I'm glad the new teacher is also kind. I look forward to continuing to work with you.

Even though it was a sudden first visit, they saw me right away and were very kind, which was a great help.

The doctor was gentle and thorough, and I would like to continue going to this clinic in the future.

I am deeply indebted to Dr. Hashimoto.

Even amidst his extremely busy schedule, he always listened attentively and showed genuine care.

Because I had a serious illness, he even went out of his way to see me on his days off.

He is truly a dedicated, kind, and reliable doctor.

I wish him all the best in his new endeavors!

My dog ​​had been prescribed an intestinal regulator and antibiotics at another hospital, but they didn't improve at all, so we switched to this hospital, where they performed tests, diagnosed him, and prescribed the correct medication, and …
There were many instances where they said they would prescribe medication but forgot, and I had to go back just to get the medication. …

I don't even want to give it a 1-star rating.
